title: Choose the visual world for SS Cleaning
question: The roll assigned the Supply-Closet Code Chart. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Supply-Closet Code Chart
options.thesis: The page is the chart pinned inside every pro cleaner's closet: each job gets its own code, and nothing gets mixed up.
options.viewport: Navy chart header with SS Cleaning, a one-line offer, and Call / Get a quote; below it three color-coded service rows start as the chart's first lines.
options.risk: Code colors beyond navy/blue must stay tags, or it drifts off Shellie's brand.

raised.raise: Every color on the page means exactly one thing; no decorative color anywhere.
The proof strip is a fixed set of four instruments, each owning one true fact: 5.0 Google, BBB A+, insured, workers' comp.
The sparkle mark appears once per view as a found landmark, never sprinkled.
Pressed and selected states invert (navy to white), never a vague shade shift.

options.label: Work Order No. 0504
options.thesis: The quote request is a real work order: numbered, checkbox services, three-part carbon copies.
options.viewport: A numbered work-order sheet with the services as checkboxes and the phone as the header line.
options.risk: The direction most trade-service runs land on; familiar to builders, but less fresh for homeowners.

options.label: Service Van Wrap
options.thesis: The page as the SS Cleaning van: phone number at door scale, services as sponsor strips along the sill.
options.viewport: Brand art breaking across two panels with a giant phone number and a gloss highlight travelling the seam.
options.case: Holds clarity (the number is unmissable) but loses on identification: a van ad, not a service to trust.
options.risk: Can read as advertising noise if the seams are not disciplined.

options.label: Mid-century Magazine Mark
options.thesis: A strict serif grid with one hidden mark per page.
options.viewport: Masthead over two columns, the mark hidden in the art.
options.case: Homeowners searching for a cleaner do not identify with magazine culture.
options.kept: One mark, used once per view.

options.label: Night Instrument Panel
options.thesis: Six gauges, each holding one truth.
options.case: Dark cockpit fights a fresh, clean promise.
options.kept: Each proof item owns exactly one fact.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.case: Novelty over trust for this audience.

options.label: Daylight Section
options.thesis: Rooms in section, lit by a travelling sunbeam.
options.viewport: A house in section with light moving through.
options.case: Beautiful, but warm gold drifts off the navy brand and the offer gets buried.

options.label: Gravity-Rain Garden
options.thesis: Color decides which way things fall.
options.case: Dreamlike surreal has no place in a cleaner's pitch.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The clean local-service landing page: photo hero, three service cards, trust row, quote form, done at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Photo hero with headline, call button and quote button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other cleaner in Summit County by design.
